Door stuck right now?

Three things to do before Darren gets there

  1. Stop pressing the opener button. If a spring or cable broke, the motor is fighting the full weight of the door and can burn out or drop it.
  2. Leave the red release cord alone unless the door is fully closed. Pulling it with the door up and a broken spring can bring the door down fast.
  3. Keep cars and kids out from under it. Then text a photo of the springs (the coils above the door) to (972) 914-9381.

Questions

Common questions

How much does a garage door repair cost?

It depends on the door and what broke. Text a photo and Darren will give you a straight estimate, and you get the written price before any work starts. The number on the quote is the number on the invoice.

Can I replace a garage door spring myself?

Please don't. Springs hold enough tension to lift a door that can weigh a few hundred pounds, and a slipped winding bar can cause serious injury. This is one repair worth calling a pro for.

Which springs does my door have?

Torsion springs sit on a metal bar above the door. Extension springs run along the tracks on each side. Snap a photo of whichever you see and send it over.

Why are the lights on my opener blinking and the door won't close?

Most of the time it's the safety sensors near the floor. Check that nothing blocks them and that both small lights are on. If one is out or flickering, they may be knocked out of line.

Do you work on all brands?

List the door and opener brands Darren services.

Are you insured? Do you warranty your work?

Yes. Peekaboo Garage Doors carries general liability and tools & equipment insurance through NEXT Insurance, and both policies are active. Ask Darren for the certificate and he'll text you the live copy before he comes out. Warranty: X years on labor, manufacturer's warranty on parts.

How do I know you're not one of the garage door scams I've read about?

Fair question. Check the business name (Peekaboo Garage Doors LLC) against the Texas Secretary of State, look for the lettered truck, and don't pay anything until the written price is approved and the work is done. If any company pressures you to pay up front or says the job tripled once they opened it up, call someone else, including us.

Do you do commercial doors?

Yes or no, from Darren.

Home / Spring Repair

Garage Door Spring Repair in Rockwall, TX

Heard a loud bang from the garage? Door suddenly too heavy to lift? That's almost always a broken spring.

Signs your spring broke

  • A loud bang from the garage, often when nobody was using the door
  • A gap in the coil of the spring above the door
  • The door feels like it weighs a ton when you lift it by hand
  • The opener strains, lifts a few inches, then stops
Stop running the opener. With a broken spring the motor is lifting the full weight of the door. It can burn out the opener or drop the door.

What Darren does

He replaces the broken spring with one matched to your door's size and weight, sets the tension, balances the door, and tests it before he leaves. If your door has two springs and one broke, the other has done the same work and is usually close behind. He'll tell you if replacing both makes sense, and you decide.

  • Single and double torsion spring replacement
  • Wood door spring replacement (heavier doors, heavier springs)
  • Conversion from old extension springs to a torsion system
  • Center and end bearing brackets, torsion tube, and cable drums when they're worn
FOR REFERENCE · Standard torsion springs are commonly rated for about 10,000 open-close cycles. Higher-cycle springs last longer for doors that run several times a day.

Home / Opener Repair

Garage Door Opener Repair and Installation

Opener hums but won't lift? Remote quit? Lights blinking? Most opener problems have a short list of causes.

Common opener problems

  • Motor hums, door doesn't move (often a broken spring, not the opener)
  • Door reverses or won't close, lights blinking (usually the safety sensors)
  • Remote or keypad stopped working
  • Opener is loud, slow, or getting old

What Darren does

He finds out whether it's the opener or the door. If the opener can be fixed, he fixes it. If it's worn out, he shows you replacement options and the price, then installs, programs your remotes and keypad, and tests the safety reverse.

  • Belt-drive openers (quiet, good for a garage under a bedroom)
  • Camera and smart openers you can run from your phone
  • Safety sensor replacement and alignment
  • Outside keypad install and programming
  • Remote programming, including car-built-in buttons

Home / Off-Track Doors

Off-Track Garage Door and Cable Repair

Door hanging crooked, a cable dangling, or rollers out of the track? Leave it where it is and call.

What not to do

Don't try to force it closed or open. An off-track door can fall. Keep cars and kids clear, and unplug the opener so nobody hits the button.

What Darren does

He secures the door, replaces snapped cables and worn rollers, straightens or replaces bent track, re-hangs the door, and balances it. Then he runs it up and down until it moves smooth and quiet.

  • Fallen door drop and secure (making a crashed door safe before repair)
  • Cable reset and rewind, cable and drum replacement
  • Full roller set replacement
  • Vertical and horizontal track repair or replacement
  • Struts for panels that sag or bow in the wind

Choosing a door

  • Steel, single or double
  • Insulated or non-insulated
  • Windows, colors and styles to match the house
